notes.1: A significant number of candidates incorrectly thought that endoplasmic reticulum was visible under high power of a light microscope. Candidates who had observed slides of plant cells were aware that the only organelles clearly visible would be chloroplasts.
notes.2: Whilst the more able candidates were able to identify the correct rows, many less able candidates incorrectly thought that transcription occurs in the rough endoplasmic reticulum.
notes.3: Almost 60% of all candidates realised that the purpose of calibrating the graticule is to use it to make measurements.
notes.4: Less than 40% of less able candidates know the characteristics of a prokaryotic cell.
notes.5: Candidates should be taught how to use a stage micrometer and eyepiece graticule.
notes.6: Whilst almost 80% of more able candidates knew that an active site was found on sucrase, over 40% of less able candidates confused hydrolysis and condensation.
notes.7: The features of triglycerides were understood by most of the more able candidates but less than 30% of the less able candidates.
notes.8: Over two thirds of less able candidates continue to have difficulty in learning the food tests.
notes.9: Biochemistry continues to be well understood by more able candidates, whilst almost 80% of the less able candidates did not know the correct answer.

notes.16: Nearly 60% of more able candidates and 70% of less able candidates did not appreciate that if water enters the stalk, from high to low water potential, the thin walled inner cells would bend more easily than the thick walled outer cells.
notes.17: Less able candidates continue to find it difficult to relate water potentials to different solute concentrations.
notes.18: Only just over 30% of candidates realised that male bees could not be genetically identical.
notes.19: Nearly 70% of all candidates answered this question correctly.

notes.22: More able candidates generally had little difficulty in processing this information. Since uracil replaces thymine in RNA, column C must be thymine. With adenine and thymine pairing up in DNA, column B must represent adenine.
notes.23: Whilst this question presented a lot of information, the more able candidates could successfully process it.
notes.24: The majority of more able candidates and almost 30% of the less able candidates correctly identified the structure of mature xylem vessel elements and a phloem sieve tube element.
notes.25: Just under half of all candidates correctly identified B as the answer. Over 45% of more able candidates selected D. D cannot be correct, since with a two dimensional image of the leaf, it is not possible to know what the surface area or volume is. Just over half of all candidates included the presence of epithelium in their answers. Epithelium is only found in animals.
notes.26: The majority of candidates were able to identify the apoplastic pathway.
notes.27: The relative difficulty of this question was due to many candidates not appreciating the processes involved in transpiration. It is the evaporation of water from mesophyll cell walls that determines rate of water movement from roots to leaves.
notes.28: Over 40% of the less able candidates did not know the difference between a closed or open circulatory system and almost 45% of them did not know the features of a double circulatory system.
notes.29: This was answered correctly by over 80% of all candidates. However, over 10% of less able candidates did not realise that the atrio-ventricular valves open and close together.
notes.30: A significant number of less able candidates and 35% of more able candidates do not know the structure of alveoli and trachea.
notes.31: It was of concern that only just over 55% of candidates understood the role of nicotine in increasing the risk of cardiac disease.
notes.32: The majority of candidates answered this correctly.
notes.33: This was not very well answered by the majority of candidates. When discussing why measles has not been eradicated by vaccination, candidates should be taught that it is a viral disease.
notes.34: Less than 40% of all candidates realised that all three reasons could cause an outbreak of malaria in a country where it had been eliminated.
notes.35: Less able candidates continue to have difficulty with the differences between the roles of T helper cells and B-lymphocytes.
notes.36: More able candidates understood the concepts of immunity much better than the less able candidates.
notes.37: Almost 40% of all candidates were able to identify the different types of white blood cell. Candidates should have looked at prepared slides of blood smears.
notes.38: Candidates found it difficult to use the data in the table to calculate the energy values for each species. The number of individuals needed to be multiplied by the biomass, then multiply this answer by the energy value. S has a value of 450 000, P a value of 1000, Q a value of 100 and R a value of 1.8.
notes.39: The percentage transfer between the Sun and producers was 1%, between the producers and primary consumers is 10%, between the primary consumers and secondary consumers is 20% and between detritus and decomposers is 80%.
notes.40: Only 30% of all candidates were able to process this information to realise that the only microorganisms that would not increase would be denitrifying bacteria which require anaerobic conditions.
notes.general_comments: General comments Three questions were answered correctly by 75% or more of candidates, these were Questions 21, 29 and 32. Ten questions were difficult with 40% or fewer candidates answering them incorrectly; Questions 1, 5, 16, 18, 27, 34, 37, 38, 39 and 40. Comments on Specific Questions A significant number of candidates incorrectly thought that endoplasmic reticulum was visible under high power of a light microscope. Candidates who had observed slides of plant cells were aware that the only organelles clearly visible would be chloroplasts.
